facts.summary: Rhode Island: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due on the next regular payday.
facts.evidence_quote: (a) Whenever an employee separates or is separated from the payroll of an employer, the unpaid wages or compensation of the employee shall become due on the next regular payday and payable at the usual place of payment.
facts.notes: Accrued vacation after one year of service is payable with final wages (same section).

facts.summary: Rhode Island: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due on the next regular payday.
facts.evidence_quote: (a) Whenever an employee separates or is separated from the payroll of an employer, the unpaid wages or compensation of the employee shall become due on the next regular payday and payable at the usual place of payment.

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Rhode Island basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $16.00.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $16.00 Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40 Time and one-half premium pay for work on Sundays and holidays in retail and certain other businesses is required under two laws that are separate from the minimum wage law.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.summary: Rhode Island: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Weekly (note 19); Bi-weekly (note 19); Semi-monthly (note 19).
facts.evidence_quote: Rhode Island: Weekly=X 19 / Bi-weekly=X 19 / Semi-monthly=X 19 / Monthly=-
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Note 19: Rhode Island. Most Rhode Island employers are required to pay employees weekly.  Childcare providers shall have the option to be paid every two weeks. Effective January 1, 2014, employers that meet certain requirements outlined in Rhode Island General Law Section 28-14-2.2 may petition the Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training for permission to pay employees less frequently than weekly but must pay wages at least twice a month. | DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.summary: Rhode Island is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration

facts.summary: Rhode Island base new employer UI rate: 1.00%.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law. Rate basis: DOL base rate. It may exclude mandatory surcharges, fund-building rates and assessments; check the state agency or total_new_employer_rate where available.

facts.summary: Rhode Island experience-rated UI tax rates range from 0.69% to 9.19%.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law. DOL prints footnote marker(s) 7 on the maximum rate. Footnote 7: tax rate shown is reduced in some circumstances due to certain UI administration or non-UI taxes paid. Footnote 8: rate year is July 1 through June 30.
